items.sentence: The frame commonly combines vertical side panels with several horizontal boards arranged one above another.
Rows of small holes along the inner sides let metal pegs support boards at chosen heights.
Some models have an open back, while others include a thin panel that stiffens the frame.
Common construction materials include solid wood, engineered wood, metal, and molded plastic.
People place reading materials on its boards, usually standing them upright or laying them in short stacks.
A user can reposition removable boards by lifting them off their supports and resetting the pegs.
Regular dusting removes particles from the horizontal surfaces and from the edges of stored items.
An installer may fasten a tall unit to a wall to reduce the chance of it tipping forward.
In a home, this furniture often stands in a study or living room near a chair or desk.
Public libraries arrange rows of these units to make collections accessible throughout reading areas.
A classroom may place one beside a work area so learners can reach reference materials during lessons.
In a small apartment, a narrow version can fit against a wall without occupying much floor space.
It keeps reading materials grouped in one place, making titles easier to locate and return after use.
Storing items upright can make their spines visible, helping readers scan a collection quickly.
Its open tiers provide storage while leaving stored materials accessible without opening doors or drawers.
By raising stored items above the floor, it can free up nearby surface area for other activities.
